title: What Happens When You Let The Voices Out Of Your Head

contact_edits.before: Musical director Wayne Gwillim musters his forces impeccably; this is as well-sung a show as you'll find in Toronto. Remaining performers include Parris Greaves as a minister, Patricia Zentilli as a surprisingly soft-boiled agent and Allie Hughes, delightful as a waitress still smitten with childish adoration of Mr. Bungee, the frog-star employer who haunts Gordon's nightmares. He's played by Juan Chioran, who must be the tallest amphibian in captivity, and who seems happiest when he's allowed to take his head off and give Gordon a pep talk. His function seems to be to help our hero back to health by persuading him that writing cheerful songs for children can be a noble pursuit, as indeed it is. The really affecting journey in the show is a musician's one. Gordon's initial attempt to write a number called Frogs Have So Much Spring, in which neither he nor anyone else can believe, finally evolves into I Feel so Much Spring and, just before that, to the show's real climax Time and Music. Lindsay Anne Black designed the ingenious set; musical arrangements, carried over from the New York original, are by another fine composer (and finer lyricist), Jason Robert Brown. - A New Brain is at the Berkeley Street Theatre until Sunday. Call 416-368-3110 for tickets and information.
